subject: Deployment security preference and evidence needs — OpenArch Medical
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Lena Foster <lena.foster@openarchmed.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap + next steps (hosting + evidence)

Hi Lena — thanks again for your time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

Summary of needs you shared
- Workload: EHR ingestion + PHI extraction for prior-authorization workflows (low-latency, high-throughput).
- Compliance drivers: HIPAA/BAA is mandatory; procurement also flagged a SOC 2 attestation and quarterly audit readiness.
- Preferred routing: primary region US-West, must support customer-managed KMS and audit logs.

Options we discussed
1) Hosted Redwood API — fastest to deploy, requires contractual BAA and we can provide SOC 2 report, but PHI handling would be through our shared-hosted environment (logical isolation).
2) Dedicated capacity — reserved GPU pools in a Redwood tenant, provides stronger isolation and support for customer KMS; better for throughput guarantees.
3) Private (VPC / on-prem) — fully customer-controlled network and storage; recommended when procurement/audit requires network isolation or air-gapped evidence.

Action items I’m tracking
- Lena: confirm whether procurement’s SOC 2 request is the full report or only scoping questions (control mapping). Also confirm whether the legal team will accept our standard BAA template or request edits.
- Alex: send a tailored evidence checklist per deployment option (I’ve attached an initial questionnaire based on today’s answers).
- Kimberly: can you review the questionnaire and add platform-level evidence (encryption at-rest, key management options, logging retention, penetration test cadence)?

Attachments: OpenArch_Security_Questionnaire_v2.pdf (initial answers from call)

Proposed timeline
- Procurement confirmation by Tue 7/17
- Follow-up technical Q&A (30m) with your infra team week of 7/24

If you’d prefer, we can draft a recommendation (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) after procurement clarifies SOC 2/BAA expectations. Happy to jump on another call.

— Alex Martinez
Principal Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0132

Thanks Alex — helpful recap. A few clarifications from procurement and security: 

1) SOC 2: procurement wants the most recent SOC 2 Type II report (not a high-level summary). If you can share the report under NDA that would be ideal.
2) BAA: legal will review your standard BAA; if there are standard redlines on data residency or subprocessors we’ll flag them.
3) Preferred deployment: at a minimum we require Dedicated capacity for production PHI workloads. OpenArch may consider Private VPC if legal pushes for network isolation during the final audit.

Questions for Redwood (please confirm):
- Can Dedicated capacity support customer-managed KMS (Azure Key Vault / AWS KMS)?
- What is the retention window for audit logs and can it be extended to 7 years for certain datasets?
- Do you provide penetration test reports and an incident response SLA?

We’ll aim to get procurement’s SOC 2 acceptance vs NDA back by Tue 7/17. Thanks — let me know if any of the above requires a short follow-up call.

Lena Foster
Head of Security & Compliance
OpenArch Medical

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-demo recap + next steps (hosting + evidence)

Alex / Markus / Lena — quick technical responses below; I’ll assemble the formal evidence package and SOC 2 delivery flow once procurement confirms NDA. 

KMS
- Dedicated: supports customer-managed keys via KMS integration for AWS and Azure. Keys are used for dataset-at-rest encryption and for disk encryption where supported by the cloud provider. Customer KMS support is available in Dedicated with an onboarding checklist (we’ll share).
- Private: full KMS control is standard; can also integrate with on-prem HSMs if required.

Audit logs & retention
- Default: 90 days of detailed token-level and route-level logs in the Console.
- Extended retention: configurable to 7 years via our logs-retention add-on (pricing depends on size). We can export logs to your S3/Azure Blob for long-term retention to meet eDiscovery or audit requirements.

SOC 2 / Pen tests / IR
- SOC 2 Type II: yes, we can provide the full report under NDA. Standard practice is to redact third-party vendor contact details; otherwise we deliver the report PDF.
- Pen testing: annual third-party pen test + quarterly internal scans; we provide the summary report and remediation timeline as part of the evidence package.
- Incident response: 1 hour initial ack, 24h incident brief to customers for Sev 1; detailed post-incident report within 5 business days. SLA can be contractually specified for Dedicated/Private agreements.

Recommended next steps for OpenArch
1) Procurement signs mutual NDA so we can deliver SOC 2 Type II (we’ll include redaction notes).
2) Proceed with Dedicated pilot: reserved capacity for PHI with customer KMS; 30-day pilot to validate throughput and logging export.
3) If legal insists on network isolation during audit: plan Private VPC as fallback — SOW and timeline estimate ~6–8 weeks.

I’ll assemble a one-page evidence matrix mapping Hosted / Dedicated / Private to the exact artifacts we can share (SOC 2, pen test, KMS configs, log exports, BAA). Expect that by EOD.

— Kimberly Park
